draft.title: The government of Sparta
card: Two kings
Sparta had two kings at the same time, from two royal families. They led the army and had religious duties.
Gerousia
The council of elders had 28 men over the age of 60, plus the two kings. It prepared proposals and acted as a court in serious cases.
Ephors
Five ephors were elected each year by the citizens. They oversaw the kings and had wide powers over daily affairs.
Assembly
The assembly was made up of Spartiate men. It voted on proposals put to it, but it did not usually debate them.
draft.remember: Power in Sparta was shared among kings, elders, ephors and citizens, so no one body held it all.

a.q: Which Spartan body was chosen by election each year?
opts: The five ephors
The two kings
The council of elders
The perioikoi
a.why: The ephors were elected each year by the citizens. The kings held their position by birth into the royal families, and the gerousia was made up of men over 60, so neither was a body chosen afresh each year.
a.clue: Think of the body with five members.

b.q: Sparta's assembly voted on a proposal from the gerousia. What does this show about how Spartan government worked?
opts: Several bodies took part in making decisions
The kings alone decided every matter of state
The ephors were removed from decisions of state
The assembly debated each proposal at length
b.why: The gerousia prepared the proposal and the assembly voted on it, so more than one body took part. The assembly did not usually debate proposals, so the option about long debate is wrong.
b.clue: One body prepared the proposal and another voted.

b.best: Several bodies took part in making decisions

problems.detail: The clue 'Think of the body with five members' gives the answer away, because only one option, 'The five ephors', names a number of five. A student can match the clue to it without knowing which body was elected.
